suggestions_catalog.message: Your resume is missing critical skills required for this role. Recruiters and ATS systems filter for these specifically.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Add each missing critical skill to your Skills section and demonstrate it in at least one project or experience bullet.
suggestions_catalog.example: Skills: Python, SQL, REST API, Git. Projects: Built a REST API with Python and Flask, backed by a PostgreSQL database.

suggestions_catalog.message: Several preferred skills for this role are absent from your resume. Including them can differentiate you from other candidates.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Add relevant preferred skills you have experience with to your Skills section, even if used briefly in a side project.
suggestions_catalog.example: Skills: Docker, AWS, CI/CD. Projects: Deployed a Flask app to AWS EC2 using a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline.

suggestions_catalog.message: No Projects section was detected. For technical roles, projects are a primary signal of hands-on ability, especially for early-career candidates.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Add a Projects section with at least two technical projects. Include the tech stack, your specific contribution, and a link to the code or demo.
suggestions_catalog.example:
Projects
• Resume Analyzer | Python, Flask, SQLite | github.com/you/resume-analyzer
  Built a REST API that parses PDF/DOCX resumes and scores them against job roles.

suggestions_catalog.message: Adding relevant certifications can boost both your resume score and ATS compatibility, particularly when formal experience is limited.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: List certifications in a dedicated Certifications section with the issuing body and year. Prioritize vendor-recognized certs relevant to the target role.
suggestions_catalog.example:
Certifications
• AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner — Amazon Web Services, 2024
• Google Data Analytics Certificate — Coursera, 2023

suggestions_catalog.message: No Work Experience or Internship section was detected. This is the most heavily weighted section for most roles.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Add an Experience section listing internships, part-time roles, freelance work, or significant volunteer positions with job title, company, dates, and bullet-point achievements.
suggestions_catalog.example:
Experience
• Software Engineering Intern — Acme Corp, Jun 2023–Aug 2023
  Developed a data pipeline in Python that reduced processing time by 40%.

suggestions_catalog.message: Your experience bullets lack quantified metrics. Numbers make accomplishments concrete and credible to both recruiters and ATS parsers.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Revise each bullet to include at least one number: percentage improvement, scale, speed, cost saving, or user count.
suggestions_catalog.example: Before: Improved the checkout flow. After: Redesigned the checkout flow, reducing cart abandonment by 18% (tracked via Google Analytics).

suggestions_catalog.message: No GitHub profile link was found. For technical roles, GitHub is often checked by hiring managers to verify your code quality and activity.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Add your GitHub profile URL to your contact header in the format: github.com/yourusername. Make sure your pinned repositories are relevant to the role.
suggestions_catalog.example: John Doe | john@example.com | +1-555-0100 | linkedin.com/in/johndoe | github.com/johndoe

suggestions_catalog.message: No LinkedIn profile link was detected. LinkedIn is the primary professional network recruiters use to verify and expand on your resume.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Add your LinkedIn URL to the contact header. Ensure your LinkedIn profile is complete and matches the resume content.
suggestions_catalog.example: John Doe | john@example.com | linkedin.com/in/johndoe | github.com/johndoe

suggestions_catalog.message: No email address was found on your resume. Email is the primary way recruiters reach out and is required by most ATS parsers.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Add a professional email address to the top of your resume. Use a format like firstname.lastname@gmail.com and avoid unprofessional handles.
suggestions_catalog.example: Jane Smith | jane.smith@gmail.com | +91-98765-43210

suggestions_catalog.message: No phone number was detected. Many recruiters call directly before emailing, and ATS systems score contact completeness.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Add a phone number to the contact section. Include the country code if applying internationally.
suggestions_catalog.example: Jane Smith | jane.smith@gmail.com | +1-415-555-0190 | linkedin.com/in/janesmith

suggestions_catalog.message: Your resume is very short and may not contain enough content for ATS systems to evaluate effectively.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Expand each section with detailed bullet points. Aim for 300–700 words total. Describe your role, technologies used, and the outcome for each position or project.
suggestions_catalog.example: Developed a REST API using Flask and PostgreSQL that served 500+ daily active users, with 99.9% uptime over 6 months.

suggestions_catalog.message: Your resume is longer than 1,500 words. Recruiters spend an average of 7 seconds on the first scan — conciseness is critical.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Trim each bullet to one strong line. Remove positions older than 10 years unless directly relevant. Aim for 300–700 words for entry/mid level; up to 900 for senior.
suggestions_catalog.example: Before (3 lines): Responsible for developing, testing, and maintaining the backend services for the company's main product using Python and Flask and also wrote unit tests... After (1 line): Built and maintained Python/Flask microservices with 90%+ test coverage.

suggestions_catalog.message: Your resume lacks strong action verbs. Bullet points starting with passive language read as weak and are less compelling to both humans and ATS.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Start every bullet point with a past-tense action verb. Replace 'Responsible for' and 'Helped with' with specific verbs that quantify ownership.
suggestions_catalog.example: Instead of: Responsible for managing the CI/CD pipeline. Write: Automated CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions, cutting deployment time by 30%.

suggestions_catalog.message: Your resume uses first-person pronouns (I, me, my) more than five times. Resumes should be written in third-person implied style.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Remove all instances of 'I', 'me', 'my', 'we', 'our'. Start bullets directly with a verb or noun. Read each sentence aloud starting with '[Your name]' to verify.
suggestions_catalog.example: Instead of: I developed a microservice that I deployed on AWS. Write: Developed and deployed a microservice on AWS, reducing latency by 20ms.

suggestions_catalog.message: Your resume lacks bullet point formatting. Paragraphs are harder for ATS systems to parse and for recruiters to scan quickly.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Convert all experience and project descriptions into concise bullet points (•, -, or *). Each bullet should cover one achievement or responsibility.
suggestions_catalog.example:
Experience
• Designed and implemented a real-time notifications system using WebSockets (Python, Redis)
• Reduced API response time by 35% through query optimization and caching with Redis
• Wrote 80+ unit and integration tests using pytest, achieving 92% code coverage

suggestions_catalog.message: A professional Summary or Objective section is missing. This is the first thing a recruiter reads and sets the tone for the entire resume.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Add a 2–3 sentence summary at the top. State your level, focus area, and one key differentiator. Tailor it to the target role.
suggestions_catalog.example: Summary: Results-driven Software Engineer with 2 years of experience building scalable Python web services. Passionate about clean architecture and automated testing. Seeking a backend role to deliver high-impact features in a product-focused team.

suggestions_catalog.message: No dedicated Skills section was found. ATS systems specifically look for a Skills section to extract and match technical keywords.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Add a Skills section with clearly labelled categories. List tools, languages, and frameworks relevant to the target role.
suggestions_catalog.example:
Skills
• Languages: Python, JavaScript, SQL
• Frameworks: Flask, React, Express
• Tools: Git, Docker, VS Code
• Databases: PostgreSQL, MongoDB

suggestions_catalog.message: No Education section was detected. Most ATS systems require an Education entry; many job applications reject resumes without one automatically.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Add an Education section with your degree, institution, and graduation year. Include GPA or relevant coursework if strong.
suggestions_catalog.example:
Education
• B.Tech in Computer Science — Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi | 2020–2024 | CGPA: 8.6/10

suggestions_catalog.message: Some of your section headings may not be recognized by ATS parsers. Non-standard headings like 'About Me' or 'What I've Done' are frequently skipped.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Rename sections to industry-standard headings: Experience, Education, Skills, Projects, Certifications, Summary. Avoid creative or informal labels.
suggestions_catalog.example: Use: 'Work Experience' not 'Where I've Worked'. Use: 'Technical Skills' not 'My Toolkit'. Use: 'Projects' not 'Things I Built'.

suggestions_catalog.message: Your resume is well-structured and scores strongly on both content quality and ATS compatibility. Focus on the specific skill gaps above to maximize your match rate.
suggestions_catalog.how_to_fix: Keep the momentum: update your resume with each new project or role within a week of completion, and tailor the Skills section slightly per application.
suggestions_catalog.example: For each new job application: copy your base resume, adjust the Summary to match the job title, and reorder the top 3 skills to mirror the job description's first paragraph.
